title: accounts/<id>.json
description: An account, open or closed. Its values are in the history files, which refer to it by ID. Closing an account sets closed and deletes nothing.

id.description: The same as the file name.

name.description: Display name; change it whenever you like.

kind.description: What kind of account it is. loan, mortgage and creditCard are debts, recorded as negative balances. The kind sets the defaults of valuation and assetClasses, and how a check-in fills in a value's flow.

currency.description: The currency of the account's balances and cash.

opened.description: The first day the account counts toward net worth.

closed.description: The last day it counts. Absent while the account is open. A closed account leaves check-ins and today's totals, keeps its values, and still shows in every chart up to that day.

valuation.description: How values are recorded. balance: one amount. holdings: positions (quantity × price) plus optional cash. trades: holdings, purchase cost and cash come from the account's trades (TRADES.md), and its valuations record only cash. Default: holdings for brokerage, crypto and metals, balance for the other kinds.

assetClasses.description: The asset mix of values recorded as a single balance, for the breakdowns and the planner: a balance account's, or the balances in a holdings account's imported history (positions follow their instruments). Default: cash for cash and savings, realEstate for property; otherwise such a value counts as other.

availableFromAge.description: The age from which plans can draw on the account, e.g. 67 for a pension fund. Until 1 January of the first year you're that age, plans keep it apart: locked, at its own mix, not wealth-taxed (PLANNER.md). Left out, it can be drawn at any age. The app suggests 65 for a new pension fund.

includeIn.description: What the account counts in. Both default to true; a primary home would normally set plan to false.

successor.description: The account that replaced this one, e.g. when you switched banks, so charts stay continuous.
